bib.title: Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning

read.skipped: Extended Data Tables 1-4 are images; read by rendering pages 10-13 and viewing them. Supplementary Discussion is not in the PDF.

question: Can a single RL agent learn successful control policies directly from raw pixels and game score across many Atari 2600 games with one algorithm, architecture and hyperparameter set?
hypothesis: Combining Q-learning with a deep convolutional network, experience replay and a periodically updated target network gives stable end-to-end learning from high-dimensional input.
contributions: Deep Q-network (DQN): convolutional Q-function trained end to end with a Q-learning variant
Experience replay and a separate, periodically cloned target network to stabilise training
Human-level-comparable performance on 49 Atari games with fixed hyperparameters

method.summary: A convolutional network maps 4 stacked 84x84 luminance frames to one Q-value per action. It is trained with Q-learning on uniformly sampled minibatches from a replay memory, with TD targets from a target network cloned every C updates. A separate network is trained per game with identical settings.
method.task: Atari 2600 game playing from pixels (Arcade Learning Environment)

datasets.name: Atari 2600 games (ALE), 49 games
datasets.size: 50M frames of training per game (about 38 days of game experience)
datasets.split: no split; hyperparameter search on 5 games (Pong, Breakout, Seaquest, Space Invaders, Beam Rider)
datasets.preprocessing: max over current and previous frame per pixel; Y channel; rescale to 84x84; stack m=4 frames; rewards clipped to [-1,1] in training; frame skip k=4; up to 30 no-op actions at episode start

other.output: linear, one per valid action, 4 to 18 actions

models.name: Best linear learner
models.architecture: linear function approximator on hand-designed features

training.objective: Q-learning squared TD error with target y = r + gamma max_a' Q(s',a';theta-), error clipped to [-1,1]
training.optimizer: RMSProp, gradient momentum 0.95, squared gradient momentum 0.95, min squared gradient 0.01 (Extended Data Table 1)
training.warmup: replay start size 50000 frames of uniform random policy (Extended Data Table 1)

other.epsilon: linear 1.0 to 0.1 over first 1,000,000 frames, then 0.1
other.hyperparameter_search: informal on 5 games, no grid search

inference.samples: 30 evaluation episodes per game, up to 5 min each, random no-op starts; one network per game, single training run apparent

metrics.name: Normalised performance
metrics.definition: 100 x (DQN score - random score)/(human score - random score)

eval.protocol: 30 episodes per game, std reported across episodes; no significance test; ablations use 10M frames, 3 learning rates, best checkpoint evaluated every 250k frames on 135k validation frames

limits: Games needing temporally extended planning, such as Montezuma's Revenge, remain a major challenge (score 0).
Reward clipping prevents distinguishing reward magnitudes and may affect performance (authors).
Replay buffer overwrites with recent transitions and samples uniformly; authors suggest prioritised sampling (prioritized sweeping) as future work.
Hyperparameters chosen by informal search on 5 games; better values conceivable; no seeds or variance across training runs reported.
Ablation uses only 5 games, 10M frames, best checkpoint, so numbers are optimistic maxima.
Human comparison: single professional tester, about 20 episodes, 2 h practice.

code.snippet: Initialize replay memory D to capacity N; Q random weights theta; target Q^ with theta- = theta; for each step: epsilon-greedy action, store (phi_t,a_t,r_t,phi_t+1) in D, sample minibatch, y_j = r_j if terminal else r_j + gamma max_a' Q^(phi_j+1,a';theta-), gradient step on (y_j - Q(phi_j,a_j;theta))^2, every C steps reset Q^ = Q
